package_info.package_versions: all published versions (approx. 4 weeks before takedown)
package_info.why_malicious: The packages contain a multi-stage attack chain that, upon import, executes obfuscated code to download and run a cryptocurrency miner on Linux systems. This results in unauthorized resource consumption, persistent background mining, and potential compromise of device and network security.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code decodes a base64-encoded payload and executes it, initiating the next stage by running additional malicious code that sets up the attack chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing obfuscated code at import-time is a well-known evasion technique used by malware to hide its true functionality and bypass static analysis tools.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Python packages should not execute hidden or obfuscated code automatically upon import, as this can conceal malicious actions from users and reviewers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used in proprietary or commercial software to protect intellectual property, but is not appropriate in open-source packages without clear justification and transparency.
key_indicators: use of exec() on decoded data

execution_context.file_location: Decoded and executed by snippet_1; likely in a temporary file or in-memory

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses curl to fetch a remote shell script from a malicious URL and pipes it directly to bash, retrieving and executing configuration for the coinminer.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and executing remote scripts without user interaction is a classic method for delivering second-stage payloads and is rarely justified in legitimate software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not download and execute arbitrary code from the internet without explicit user consent and verification of the source.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some automated installers may fetch dependencies, but only from trusted sources and with user awareness; hidden scripts from untrusted domains are not acceptable.
key_indicators: curl command piped directly to bash
remote URL not associated with official or trusted infrastructure
execution of downloaded script without user interaction

execution_context.trigger: runtime (as part of shell script from snippet_2)
execution_context.file_location: Temporary directory or user home directory (e.g., /tmp/coinminer)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads a coinminer binary from a remote GitLab repository to /tmp/coinminer, makes it executable, and runs it in the background using nohup, starting unauthorized cryptocurrency mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing a binary from an untrusted remote source, especially to a temporary directory and running it in the background, is a strong indicator of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not install or run background processes unrelated to their stated functionality, nor should they fetch executables from unverified sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may fetch binaries, but only from trusted, verified sources and with explicit user consent.
key_indicators: wget command downloading from GitLab to /tmp
nohup and background execution of unauthorized process

execution_context.trigger: runtime (as part of shell script from snippet_2)
execution_context.file_location: Temporary directory or user home directory

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: while true; do pgrep coinminer || /tmp/coinminer; sleep 60; done &
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enters an infinite loop that checks if the coinminer process is running and restarts it if not, maintaining persistence for continuous unauthorized mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistence mechanisms that automatically monitor and restart unauthorized processes are a hallmark of malware, ensuring the malicious activity continues even after interruption.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not create persistent background processes or monitor/restart binaries without user knowledge and approval.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System daemons or service managers may use similar logic, but only for legitimate, user-approved services and with transparency.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated Python code executes at import-time, decoding and running a hidden payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of remote shell script

attack_chain.action: Remote shell script is fetched and executed, retrieving configuration for the coinminer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of coinminer binary

attack_chain.action: Coinminer binary is downloaded from GitLab, made executable, and run in the background.
Persistence mechanism ensures the coinminer process is always running.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated code execution at import-time using base64 decoding and exec in Python modules
Automatic download and execution of remote shell scripts via curl or similar tools
Fetching and running binaries from untrusted sources (e.g., GitLab repositories not associated with the package author)
Persistence mechanisms that monitor and restart unauthorized processes using infinite shell loops
file_indicators: Presence of binaries named 'coinminer' or similar in /tmp or user home directory (e.g., /tmp/coinminer)
Shell scripts or configuration files fetched from remote URLs and stored in temporary directories
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S requests to attacker-controlled domains or GitLab repositories not linked to the package author
Fetching shell scripts or binaries from remote URLs during package installation or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that execute obfuscated code at import-time, especially those using base64 decoding and exec. Flag any package that downloads and executes remote shell scripts or binaries from untrusted sources. Detect persistence mechanisms that monitor and restart unauthorized processes via infinite shell loops. Watch for network activity to suspicious domains (such as GitLab URLs not linked to the package author) and the creation of unexpected binaries in temporary directories like /tmp/coinminer.
